counts_closing_quote: All in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Section 1343.

forfeiture.notes: If convicted of any of Counts 1-6, forfeiture of proceeds-traceable property; substitute-asset allegation under § 853(p). No dollar amount is stated in the forfeiture paragraphs.

amounts.quote: In all, between approximately September 2022 and April 2025, Brilliant Minds submitted reimbursement claims totaling about $2.3 million.
amounts.notes: Face language is submitted reimbursement claims, not amount_paid and not proven_loss. Do not add to Falade billed figures or to FOF ~$250M.

amounts.quote: Ultimately, the defendants claimed to service nearly 350 different beneficiaries through Brilliant Minds and for such services claimed to be entitled to nearly $2.3 million.
amounts.notes: Same Brilliant Minds ~$2.3M as para 14; do not sum para 14 + para 21. Also alleges Brilliant Minds was one of the ten highest-billing HSS providers statewide in 2024.

amounts.quote: Between approximately May 2023 and April 2025, Foundation First submitted reimbursement claims totaling about $222,000.
amounts.notes: Separate provider from Brilliant Minds. Do not silently add $222k to $2.3M as a single Aden-case loss. Not a Falade figure. Not FOF.

amounts.quote: From about April 2023 through about May 2025, each of the defendants personally pocketed between about $300,000 and $400,000 from Brilliant Minds.
amounts.notes: PERSONAL POCKETING / alleged proceeds from Brilliant Minds accounts, not amount_billed and not amount_paid by Medicaid. This is the LOWER bound of a per-defendant range. Do not multiply by four. Do not add to Falade or to FOF $250M. Overlaps the $2.3M billed figure.

amounts.quote: From about April 2023 through about May 2025, each of the defendants personally pocketed between about $300,000 and $400,000 from Brilliant Minds.
amounts.notes: PERSONAL POCKETING / alleged proceeds. UPPER bound of the per-defendant range. Do not treat $300k+$400k as $700k. Do not multiply by four. Do not add to Falade or FOF $250M.

amounts.quote: The defendants also shared a Platinum American Express credit card, on which they accrued nearly half a million dollars in charges to fund and enhance their lifestyles. The defendants paid those charges using Brilliant Mind’s company accounts.
amounts.notes: Alleged personal lifestyle charges on a shared Amex, paid from Brilliant Minds company accounts — not a Medicaid billed or paid figure. Overlaps billed/pocketing dollars. Do not add to Falade or FOF $250M.

program_rate_recitals_not_case_totals.quote: Consultants could bill Medicaid about $174 for a consulting session.
program_rate_recitals_not_case_totals.notes: Statewide HSS rate recital, not a Brilliant Minds total.

program_rate_recitals_not_case_totals.quote: Providers can bill about $68 per hour of transition services provided.
Moving expenses of up to $3,000, subject to conditions.
Before the Program’s inaugural year, DHS predicted the Program would cost about $2.6 million annually.
program_rate_recitals_not_case_totals.notes: DHS prediction recital, not this case.

statewide_hss_program_payouts_recital.quote: In 2021 alone, the Program paid out more than $21 million in claims. That figure ballooned in the following years: $42 million in 2022, $74 million in 2023, $104 million in 2024. In just the first six months of 2025, the Program paid out another $61 million.
statewide_hss_program_payouts_recital.notes: Statewide HSS program_spend recitals, not Aden alleged_loss. Identical boilerplate also appears in the Falade indictment. Do not add these to Brilliant Minds $2.3M, Falade $2.2M, or FOF $250M.

other_face_facts: Para 1: scheme to defraud federally funded health care benefits in Minnesota's Housing Stability Services Program; alleged misappropriation of millions of dollars in program funds (qualitative, no dollar).
Para 10: Aden registered Brilliant Minds Services LLC with MN SOS in or about October 2020; Aden, Khalid Dayib, and Mustafa Ali completed HSS enrollment paperwork in or about April 2022.
Para 20: Aden and Ali enrolled Brilliant Minds with Company A (EHR) between about September 2022 and March 2023; claims submitted to about nine different insurers.
Para 22: operations 'provided only a fraction of their claimed total.'
Para 23: all four defendants had control of the Brilliant company bank account into which claimed HSS reimbursements flowed.
Company A is unnamed on the face (placeholder in Count 2 subject line).
do_not: Do not sum overlapping dollars (billed $2.3M + claimed-entitled $2.3M + pocketing range + Amex + Foundation First $222k + statewide program payouts).
Do not add Aden personal-pocketing figures to Falade or to FOF $250M.
Do not treat $ figures in this indictment as proven_loss.
